He wanted to choose the best barley from few samples.

textes.Marin Mersenne, moine de l'ordre des Min: Marin Mersenne, a monk of the Minim order, wants to say everything about sound in a single work: how it is born, how it travels, how the ear receives it. He states the laws of vibrating strings: a string sounds higher when it is shortened, tightened or thinner. He also measures the speed of sound, first by timing the delay between the flash of a gunshot and its bang, then with echoes. The book reviews the instruments of his time, from the organ to the lute, with detailed engravings. It is a great inventory, halfway between physics and a treatise on music.
textes.C'est l'un des premiers livres à traiter: It is one of the first books to treat music as an object of physical measurement.
textes.Mersenne servait de boîte aux lettres à: Mersenne acted as the mailbox of learned Europe: he circulated the work of Descartes, Fermat and many others.
textes.Un moine qui chronomètre des coups de fe: A monk timing gunshots. The AI approves of the method, less of the neighbors.
textes.Guido, moine bénédictin, enseigne le cha: Guido, a Benedictine monk, teaches singing at the cathedral school of Arezzo. Bishop Theodaldus commissions this treatise from him. In it he explains how to sing in tune, how to divide a melody and how to make two voices sing together. Above all, he champions a system of horizontal lines, a third apart, where each note has a fixed place. A red line marks F, a yellow one C. A singer can then read a melody he has never heard: it is the direct ancestor of our staff.
textes.La portée rend la musique transmissible: The staff makes music transmissible without a teacher: you read instead of learning by heart.
textes.La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears his name, but it only spread after his death.

textes.Boèce, homme d'État romain au service du: Boethius, a Roman statesman serving King Theodoric, gathers the musical knowledge of the Greeks in Latin. For him, music is first a science of numbers: the octave matches the 2/1 ratio, the fifth 3/2, the fourth 4/3. He distinguishes three musics: that of the world, the harmony of the stars and seasons; that of man, the accord of soul and body; and that of instruments, the only one you can hear. He also tells the legend of Pythagoras and the blacksmith's hammers. Throughout the Middle Ages, this book is the reference of schools and universities.
textes.C'est par lui que l'Europe médiévale app: It is through him that medieval Europe learns the Pythagorean ratios of intervals.
textes.Boèce écrit plus tard, en prison, la Con: Boethius later writes, in prison, The Consolation of Philosophy, before being executed around 524.

textes.Zarlino, élève d'Adrian Willaert et futu: Zarlino, a pupil of Adrian Willaert and future chapel master of St. Mark's in Venice, puts Renaissance music in order. He accepts as consonances the major third (5/4), the minor third (6/5) and the major sixth (5/3), which Pythagorean tuning did not know in this form. He justifies them by the first six numbers, which he calls the senario: a string is divided into two, three, four, five or six equal parts. He renumbers the modes, putting first the Ionian, our major scale, and gives detailed rules for writing in several voices and for setting words to music. His ideas pave the way for the major and minor scales of the following centuries.
textes.Il fait de l'accord avec tierce le cœur: He makes the chord with a third the heart of Western music.
textes.Son ancien élève Vincenzo Galilei, père: His former pupil Vincenzo Galilei, Galileo's father, would fiercely attack his tuning system in several pamphlets.
textes.L'élève qui contredit le maître, puis le: The pupil who contradicts the master, then the son who contradicts the Church. The AI admires the family tradition.
textes.Helmholtz est médecin, physiologiste et: Helmholtz is a physician, physiologist and physicist. He wants to understand why certain notes sound good together. With resonators, hollow cavities each tuned to one frequency, he picks out the harmonics of a sound one by one and estimates their strength. He shows that an instrument's timbre comes from the mix of these harmonics. He explains dissonance by beats: when two neighboring harmonics rub together, the sound seems rough. When they coincide, on the contrary, the chord sounds consonant. The book links physics, anatomy and music theory for the first time.
textes.Il donne une explication physique au tim: He gives a physical explanation of timbre and consonance that is still taught.
textes.Alexander Ellis l'a traduit en anglais e: Alexander Ellis translated it into English in 1875 under the title On the Sensations of Tone, and it is mostly cited under that name.
textes.Des bouteilles creuses contre l'oreille,: Hollow bottles against the ear, in the name of science. The AI has seen stranger fashions.
textes.Rameau, organiste, veut ramener l'harmon: Rameau, an organist, wants to reduce harmony to natural principles, like a physicist. He states that a chord keeps its identity whatever the order of its notes: C-E-G, E-G-C and G-C-E are the same chord, inverted. Beneath the music, he imagines a fundamental bass, an imaginary sequence of roots that carries the chord progressions, even when you cannot hear it. He establishes a hierarchy of cadences, which structures tonal music. Misunderstood on its release, the book stirs opposition, then becomes the grammar of classical harmony.
textes.Les notions d'accord renversé et de bass: The notions of inverted chords and fundamental bass, learned at the conservatory, come from here.
textes.Rameau n'a donné son premier opéra, Hipp: Rameau only staged his first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, at fifty: he was a theorist long before he was famous.
textes.Cinquante ans pour passer de la théorie: Fifty years to go from theory to the stage. The AI does both at the same time.
textes.Werckmeister, organiste en Allemagne, s': Werckmeister, an organist in Germany, tackles an old problem: twelve pure fifths do not land back on the octave. With the old tuning, some keys sounded so out of tune that they were avoided. In his best-known tuning, he spreads the gap over four slightly narrowed fifths and keeps the other eight pure: every key becomes playable, each with its own color. These solutions are called unequal temperaments, or “well temperaments.” They are the first steps toward a keyboard where you can change key without fearing a glaring wrong note.

textes.Oliver Sacks, neurologue, raconte des ca: Oliver Sacks, a neurologist, tells of cases where music and the brain meet in strange ways. A surgeon struck by lightning suddenly discovers a consuming passion for the piano. Frozen patients with Parkinson's disease regain movement thanks to rhythm. A musician deprived of recent memory forgets everything within seconds, except music, which he still plays perfectly. He also writes about the musical hallucinations that sometimes come with deafness, and about perfect pitch. Each story shows that music engages almost the whole brain.

textes.La hauteur suit la fréquence. L'amplitud: Pitch follows frequency. Amplitude changes the intensity, not the pitch.
textes.Un son plus fort est forcément plus aigu: A louder sound is necessarily higher.
